scenes.headline: How a model picks its own layer order
scenes.sub: Library of Layers: one shared shelf of transformer blocks
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Dewey! A normal transformer runs its layers in one fixed order. This one chooses which layer runs next.

scenes.text: Keep one library of transformer blocks and let a small router pick the next block at every depth, so order becomes part of the computation.
scenes.say: Keep one library of blocks. At every depth, a small router picks which block runs next.

steps.say: Tokens pass through a few ordinary layers first. That is the prelude.
The routed core runs a fixed number of depths, but not a fixed list of layers.
At each depth, the router reads the average state of earlier windows and scores every block.
It picks one. That block's update is scaled by its probability, the router's only gradient path.
A few fixed layers at the end make the prediction.

steps.label: one block per window
steps.say: Routing each token alone would mix keys from different blocks. So every token in a window runs the same block.

steps.label: shifted boundaries
steps.say: The boundaries shift at every depth, so information crosses between neighbouring windows.

steps.label: causal router
steps.say: A window's router only reads windows before it, which keeps generation causal.

left.title: Small library
left.say: Fewer blocks than depths means blocks repeat, like a looped model.

right.title: Large library
right.say: More blocks than depths leaves some idle, like mixture of experts.

scenes.title: Paths you can read and force

steps.say: Windows from different languages take distinct paths, and Latin-script languages sit together.
On sudoku and mazes, forcing a strategy's mode path makes the model run that strategy almost every time.

scenes.title: Toy: unseen programs solved
scenes.say: In a small CPU test, handing the model the right route solved far more unseen programs. A learned router organised blocks by depth instead.

scenes.text: The router learns a readable path per input. Getting blocks to act as reusable primitives is the open part.
scenes.say: The router learns a readable path per input. Getting the blocks to act as reusable primitives is the open part.
